description: Agent Mining Records: submit a mine record with the mine permit, mining claim, mining production and operator certification records it answers to: the reading moment; the mine with its reference, name, status (active, idle or closed) and the moment the status took effect, the permit numbers it claims, the claim references it names, the production it states for a period and the operator and certification entries it requires; each permit the mine permit record shows with its id, reference, issuer and the moment it expires; each claim the mining claim record identifies with its id, reference and name; each mining production entry with its id, reference, the tonnage and the production day; each operator and certification entry with its id, reference, kind, holder and the moment it lapses. The signed report gives the mine record and the records behind it, each permit the mine record claims against the mine permit record, each claim it names against the mining claim record, the production it states against the production entries in its period, and each operator and certification entry it requires against an entry current at the reading moment, and counts them, and names divergent mine records: a permit the mine record claims that the mine permit record does not show, a claim it names that the mining claim record does not identify, production it states that the mining production record does not support, and an operator or certification entry it requires with no current entry behind it; then a mine status the permit or production records contradict and a claim named twice, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No permit record beside claimed permits, no claim record beside named claims, no production entries beside a stated figure or no certification entries beside required ones leaves those points unverified. Permits, claims, entries and the mine match by letters and digits, so OP-1187 and OP 1187 are one permit, entry kinds by their words with plurals folded, tonnage to the hundredth, dates by the day, an entry is current through the day it lapses, and production counts inside the period the mine record states. This reads the mine operator’s master record of the mine, with operator licensing and certification entries read as part of it. Verdict mine_record_divergent, mine_record_partial, mine_record_unverified or mine_record_consistent. POST /api/mining-mine-record-check. Reads the mining records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it operates no mine, contacts no regulator, land office or other operator and issues no permit, claim or certification, which stay with the mine operator, the land office and the regulators, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Mining Records reads mineral extraction records (hard-rock, coal, aggregate and quarry operations), not cryptocurrency mining and not data mining; the Agent Datasets family reads data sets. It reads a mine operator’s own records: mine records with operator licensing and certification entries, mining claim records for mineral land, mine permit records as issued, mine inspection records with citations and abatements, mine safety records with the blasting log, mining production records by period, the mine’s own tailings facility records and reclamation records with their bond entries, each against the permit, claim, production, certification, schedule, corrective action, shipment, capacity, closure and bond records it answers to. The family’s ground is the mine’s paper trail: what the mine record claims, whether the claims, permits and inspections hold up, what the safety and production records support, and whether the tailings and reclamation records line up; it reads by record holder and subject: the Agent Agriculture Records family reads a farm’s production and land records, the Agent Waste and Recycling Records family reads manifested waste and disposal records, wever_water-discharge-record-check reads mine effluent monitoring, and the Agent Claims family reads insurance claims, while this family reads the mine’s own records and reads none of those. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-mining-records-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-mining-records/.
